clue.text: Boring outside broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters of the preceding word are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: An outside broadcast on television that turns out to be dull viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the TV phrase 'outside broadcast' but it tells you to rearrange OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is tiresome and dull, exactly what boring means as an adjective.

clue.text: Adopt the company policy and defend it strongly?

parts.note: to adopt something is to take it on
a firm is a company; 'the' gives the article A
a stand is a stated position or policy

explanation.surface: An employee decides to adopt the company line and argue fiercely for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link between the wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a firm stand means holding your position resolutely, defending it strongly against opposition.

clue.text: Masonic bed where the going's always good!

definitions.meaning: a layer laid in masonry, a bed in the bricklaying sense, to stop rising damp
read as a racecourse, the going, or ground condition, would never be spoilt by rain

explanation.definitionFit: It is the waterproof layer in a brick wall, and also read as a racetrack that rain could never soak.

clue.text: Expenditure needed to win the Bricklayers' Championship?

definitions.text: needed to win the Bricklayers' Championship?
definitions.meaning: read as a verb, to ... is to lay bricks better than everyone else

explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent, and taken whimsically it also means laying more bricks than the rivals.

clue.text: Top military medal — and properly attired to receive it

indicators.note: to receive it says the dress piece takes in the medal, holding it inside

parts.note: a suit is what one wears to be properly attired
MM is the abbreviation for the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A top military medal is awarded to someone who has dressed smartly to collect it.
explanation.walkthrough: MM goes into SUIT; 'and' is a link. 'Top military medal' looks like a single phrase, but 'Top' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point of a mountain, its top.

clue.text: Spooner's stuff, sailor's vehicle

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
a tar is a sailor, an old nickname; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Some odd belongings and a seaman's means of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of CRAM and TAR gives TRAM and CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a passenger vehicle running on rails along the street.

clue.text: 23s turned up in support for driver — watch the reaction here!

indicators.note: in places the turned-up word inside the golf support

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball for a driver shot

indicators.note: turned up, in a down entry, means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: 23 is the cross-reference to the fool at 23 across; fools are butts of jokes

explanation.surface: A golfer's tee gets jokers turned up inside it as a chemistry experiment is watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down entry, read bottom to top. The driver is a golf club, not a motorist; 23s are fools, here butts of jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is the glass vessel in a laboratory where a chemical reaction can be watched.

clue.text: Coming our way, property's in a position noticed coming up

parts.note: a lie is a position, as in the lie of a golf ball

indicators.note: coming up, in a down entry, means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: noticed means seen

explanation.surface: Property is coming our way, its position spotted as it approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns SEEN into NEES; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienees are the legal recipients of property transferred to them, so we would be alienees when property comes our way.

clue.text: Fulfil obligation, as diver would have to with flea in his suit?

definitions.text: as diver would have to with flea in his suit?
definitions.meaning: a deep-sea diver itching from a flea would need to surface in order to scratch

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to reach the expected standard, and literally describes a diver rising to the surface to scratch.

clue.text: Receiver signs for this on the point before/after collecting daughter

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
the gist is the main point

indicators.note: collecting says the pair of words take the daughter between them

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before and ... is Latin for after

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a parcel signs at the point before or after a daughter is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' places the daughter at the slash, between the two halves of 'before/after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Registered post is the mail service in which the recipient must sign for the delivered item.

clue.text: Tidy £1,000 not completely spent

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in £10K

indicators.note: not completely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: spent, as of a supply used up, means empty

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a thousand pounds neatly, though they have nearly used it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' trims EMPTY to EMPT. KEMPT is the rare positive of unkempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Kempt means neatly kept or combed, the opposite of unkempt, so it is a synonym of tidy.

clue.text: "Play Misty for Me" in clubs, with force — as broadcaster in future?

indicators.note: play, as of a part, means put through motions, here telling us to rearrange the letters of Misty

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
G is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: Someone requests the film Play Misty for Me at a nightclub, forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like part of the film title but is the anagram signal; 'for', 'in' and 'with' are links. MYSTIC MEG was a British tabloid and TV astrologer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystic Meg was a well-known British astrologer who broadcast forecasts on the National Lottery show, telling of the future.

clue.text: Inspired unintelligibility, say

parts.note: inspired here means moved by the Holy Spirit; the phrase describes the ecstatic utterance of words no listener can understand

explanation.surface: Speech that is moved by inspiration but makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' hints at the speaking that the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossolalia, the religious practice of uttering unknown languages in ecstatic worship, is inspired and unintelligible speech.

clue.text: See 1
On the fiddle or on the hoof

definitions.meaning: the part at the heel of a violin bow, held by the player
the elastic horny pad on the underside of a horse's hoof

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a part of the violin bow and the pad in a horse's hoof.

clue.text: Directed a worker to go out in shower? No

indicators.note: to go out, meaning to go outside, says that the worker piece wraps around the directed piece

parts.note: a worker bee is the commonest crossword worker
directed, as of someone sent somewhere, means sent

explanation.surface: Someone was told to send a worker outside into the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEE goes outside SENT; 'in' is a link. The definition reads 'shower' as one who shows up: an absentee is a no-show.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower in the cryptic sense is someone who shows up; an absentee is the opposite, a person who fails to appear.

clue.text: Corrects orders for literature periods spent in Bible class

indicators.note: spent in says the periods are what is spent in the class, following after it

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school class where the Bible is studied
spells are periods of time

explanation.surface: Literature periods are given over to Bible study, and orders are corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'literature' as letters: to respell is to put letters in better order. RE is Religious Education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To respell is to spell again, correcting the order of letters in written words.

clue.text: Messing up rondo in pub, I can't be missed

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: messing up means jumbling the letters of rondo

explanation.surface: A rondo is botched in a pub, and the performer is unmissable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The definition speaks as the door: a barn door is proverbially too big to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Barn door is used of a target so large no one could miss it, as in 'couldn't hit a barn door'.

clue.text: Soldier's rejected tree lover

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the tree is written backwards

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A soldier has been turned down by someone who loves trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Soldier stands for 'is', a link; leman is an archaic word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is an infantry soldier armed with a rifle, often the rank of private in rifle regiments.

clue.text: It's clear near to 10's heart, say

indicators.note: say tells us the picked letters are to be spoken, not spelt

parts.note: 10 is the astrologer's name at 10 across; its heart, the middle letter, is I, and the letter beside it is C

explanation.surface: Something is plain to someone close to the fortune teller's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you the two letters are spoken, giving the phrase meaning 'understood'.
explanation.definitionFit: I see is said when something has become clear to you: it means you understand.

clue.text: Viewer's fortune's not quite on the up during row

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is set inside the row piece

parts.note: to row is to pull an oar

indicators.note: on the up, in a down entry, means read upwards, backwards
not quite drops the last letter

parts.note: fortune means luck; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A spectator's fortune is nearly on the rise during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel but is the oarsman's verb; 'on the up' suits a down entry, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye, the organ that does the viewing, so it means of a viewer.

clue.text: Unit is anyhow positioned as intended

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, haphazard way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A unit is somehow positioned in the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original place, where it was meant to be.

clue.text: Very quiet mall?

parts.note: very quiet in music is pianissimo, PP, and those letters sit at the middle of the word for going to the shops

explanation.surface: A deserted shopping mall.
explanation.walkthrough: PP, the musical mark for very quiet, is the centre of SHOPPING, while the whole phrase is a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping centre is a large indoor complex of shops, which Americans call a mall.

clue.text: See 8
Gowk in springtime, playing polo with flair

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being toyed with and shuffled

explanation.surface: A fool in spring plays polo stylishly.
explanation.walkthrough: POLO and FLAIR rearrange to give the answer; 'with' is a link. A gowk is a Scots word for a fool, and an April gowk is a victim of a 1 April prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowk is Scots for a fool, and the fool made on the first day of April in spring is exactly this.

clue.text: Opening location of the Iliad, but not the ending

indicators.note: but not the ending says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Homer's Iliad is set at the siege of Troy, so its action takes place in Troy

explanation.surface: The Iliad begins at Troy, though it lacks a proper ending.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TROY loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Furniture seen backstage by actor

definitions.meaning: a sideboard or kitchen cabinet with shelves for dishes
a theatre assistant who helps an actor into costume behind the scenes

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a piece of kitchen furniture, and the theatre assistant who helps actors put on their costumes.

clue.text: In the round, one place to see watering animals squat?

indicators.note: In says the letter for one goes inside the shifted word
the round suggests letters going round, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a trough is where animals drink
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In a circle, one location for watching animals drinking that is crouching low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the round' sends the T of TROUGH to the end, ROUGHT, and 'In' puts I inside before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To rough it is to live without comforts, as a squatter might, so squat stands for the idea of roughing it.
